steps.body: x² = −1 has no real solution — every real number squares to zero or more. Mathematicians' fix: invent a new number. Define **i** by **i² = −1**. With it, square roots of negatives make sense: √(−9) = √9 · √(−1) = **3i**.
i is a quarter turn, not a mystery.

widget.prompt: w = i. Find the z whose product z × i lands on −2.
widget.successFeedback: z = 2i. Multiplying by i turns the arrow a quarter turn anticlockwise — and 2i was already a quarter turn from 2, so the product has been turned a HALF turn onto the negative real axis. That is the only honest reason i² = −1: two quarter turns leave you facing backwards.
widget.realFeedback: The product lands in the wrong spot along the real axis. Multiplying by i rotates the arrow 90°, so it is a z ON the imaginary axis that lands on the real one.
widget.imagFeedback: The real part is right, but the product still has an imaginary part left over. The target is −2 exactly, sitting flat on the real axis.

predict.prompt: Multiplying by i spins a number a quarter-turn counterclockwise. To LAND on −2 (pointing left), z must start out pointing…
predict.reveal: A quarter-turn counterclockwise carries 'up' to 'left': z = 2i spins to 2i · i = 2i² = −2. Multiplying by i never stretches anything — it only turns.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents i def.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for i def must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines i def.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

steps.body: The rule in general: **√(−k) = i√k** for k > 0 — pull the −1 out as i, then root the rest. And equations follow: x² = −16 now HAS solutions, x = ±4i, because (4i)² = 16 · i² = −16 and (−4i)² does the same.

explanationVariants: Pull out the −1 as i: i√49 = 7i.

commonBuilds.feedback: (−7)² = +49, not −49 — no real number works; the answer needs i.
The root still applies to 49: √49 = 7, so 7i.
(−7i)² does equal −49 too, but the radical symbol names the PRINCIPAL root: 7i.

widget.missFeedback: √(−49) = √49 · √(−1) — the 7 comes out real, the i carries the negative.
widget.successFeedback: Right — 7 from the 49, i from the −1.

widget.prompt: What are the solutions of x² = −16?

options.label: x = ±4
options.feedback: (±4)² = +16 — that solves x² = 16. The minus needs i: ±4i.

options.label: x = 4i only
options.feedback: (−4i)² = 16i² = −16 as well — squaring kills the sign, so BOTH ±4i solve it.

options.label: no solutions
options.feedback: That was true before i existed — there are no REAL solutions, but the complex pair ±4i solves it exactly.

explanationVariants: i is DEFINED by i² = −1 — everything else about complex numbers flows from that.
By definition, squaring i lands on −1.

commonBuilds.feedback: If i² were 1, i would just be ±1 and nothing new — the whole point is i² = −1.
A number equal to its own square would satisfy x² = x, so x = 0 or 1 — i is neither.
i² is real: the definition says it equals −1, not another imaginary number.

widget.missFeedback: i is DEFINED so that squaring it gives −1.
widget.successFeedback: Right — that's the definition of i.

explanationVariants: Square the 3 and the i separately: 9 and −1, product −9.

commonBuilds.feedback: That drops i² = −1 — the imaginary unit flips the sign: −9.
Squaring removes the i entirely: i² = −1 is real, so (3i)² = −9 is real.
That's 3i doubled and negated — squaring means 3i × 3i = 9i² = −9.

widget.missFeedback: Square both parts: 3² = 9 and i² = −1, so (3i)² = −9.

explanationVariants: Square first — the i² turns 25 negative — then add 30.

commonErrors.feedback: That treats (5i)² as +25 — but i² = −1 makes it −25, and −25 + 30 = 5.
Two sign slips: (5i)² = −25, then ADD the 30: −25 + 30 = +5.

hints: Square the 5 and the i separately.

steps.body: i is the number whose square is −1 — it unlocks roots of negatives.
takeaways: √(−k) = i√k: pull the −1 out as i.
steps.teaser: Next: what happens when you keep multiplying by i — a four-step cycle.

concept.body: √(−k) splits into √k times i. For √(−36): √36 = 6, so the answer is 6i.

explanationVariants: 6 from the 36, i from the minus sign.

options.feedback: (−6)² = +36 — a real square can't be negative; the i is required.

options.label: 36i
options.feedback: Still take the root of 36: it's 6i.

options.label: 18i
options.feedback: 18 is 36 ÷ 2 — the ROOT of 36 is 6, so 6i.
